name: Graiguesallagh
agent: Enda Smith, Sherry FitzGerald Brady O'Flaherty, Celbridge
questions: What is the business in the large shed with signage that shares the western boundary, what are its hours, and does it bring lorries or deliveries past the gate on the R408?

Bedroom 3 (3.58 × 2.11 m) opens only off the living room. Would you or the vendors know whether the cut-stone outbuildings have been assessed for conversion to a self-contained annex, and has any pre-planning been done with Kildare County Council?
What are the water supply and drainage (mains water or a well; septic tank or treatment unit, and its age and certification)? The listing only states oil-fired central heating.
Can you send the full BER certificate (119712164)? Is it E1 or E2, what is the kWh/m²/yr, and were the walls or roof of the original house insulated when it was extended about 20 years ago?
Is the house or the outbuildings on Kildare's Record of Protected Structures or the NIAH, and has a radon test been done (BuyerIQ flags moderate radon risk)?

ai.why: A genuine early-1800s agent's house with a cut-stone courtyard on 2.2 acres, 8–12 minutes from Maynooth's Dublin trains, with three bathrooms and a ground-floor bedroom by an accessible shower. Held back by 133 m² and small common rooms for six, a tiny walk-through ground-floor bedroom, a commercial premises on the west boundary, BER E and €595k.

electricity.detail: Likely connected; not stated, but the house is lived in, alarmed, and has an electronic gate.

water.detail: Not stated. A rural roadside site: could be mains or a private well; ask.

sewer.detail: Not stated. Probably a septic tank on a rural site like this; ask its age and certification.

internet.detail: Full fibre at the address per BuyerIQ ('Fast broadband — 392 Mb full fibre'); the listing doesn't mention broadband and the provider isn't confirmed.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Bedroom 3 (3.58 × 2.11 m, cast-iron fireplace) is on the ground floor but opens only off the living room; the ground-floor bathroom (1.84 × 2.46 m, accessible walk-in shower) is across the house off the rear hallway, so it is a small single and walk-through, not a parents' suite. The cut-stone outbuildings are the realistic annex route, subject to planning.

bedsNote: Two en-suite doubles upstairs; Bedroom 3 is a small ground-floor single (3.58 × 2.11 m) off the living room
heating: Oil-fired central heating, plus a stove in the kitchen and original cast-iron fireplaces
tagline: An early-1800s stone house, built for the Duke of Leinster's land agent, with a gravelled courtyard of cut-stone outbuildings and a 2.2-acre paddock on the R408 about 6 km south-west of Maynooth.

pros.detail: Early-1800s house built for the Duke of Leinster's land agent, in one family for five generations: stone walls, a gabled Gothic-window porch, decorative bargeboards and original cast-iron fireplaces in the living room and Bedroom 3.

About 0.89 ha behind an electric gate: a gravelled rear courtyard ringed by cut-stone outbuildings with timber doors, mature hedges and a paddock for the dogs; the agent says the outbuildings could suit residential use, subject to consents.
Maynooth station is about 6.8 km by road: roughly half-hourly trains to Connolly in 36–44 minutes, some running on to Pearse; St Stephen's Green is about 35 minutes by car via the M4.

pros.text: Three bathrooms, one on each sleeping floor
pros.detail: Two en-suites upstairs (one 3.40 × 2.88 m with an inset bath) plus a ground-floor bathroom with an accessible walk-in shower; Daft's header '1 bath' undercounts.

pros.text: Maynooth town and good schools close
pros.detail: Maynooth's shops, university town centre and Maynooth Post Primary are about 6 km; Rathcoffey NS (231 pupils, mixed) is 2 km and is a named feeder to Maynooth Post Primary.

pros.text: Lets well near Dublin and Maynooth University
pros.detail: A characterful house 35 minutes from Dublin and 7 minutes from a university town should let easily when the family is away.

cons.text: Small for six: 133 m², three beds
cons.detail: Living room 3.58 × 4.37 m (15.6 m²) and kitchen/dining 4.92 × 4.42 m (21.7 m²) are the only common rooms; well below the 180–280 m² the family wants, so an extension or outbuilding conversion is likely needed.

cons.text: Ground-floor bedroom is a tiny walk-through single
cons.detail: Bedroom 3 is 3.58 × 2.11 m and opens only off the living room, with the accessible shower room across the hall; fine for a short stay, not a permanent parents' room.

cons.text: Commercial premises on the west boundary
cons.detail: The listing aerials show a large shed with shop signage, a forecourt and parked cars directly beside the house and courtyard; the business wasn't identified. A farm shed with wrapped bales sits across the lane at the paddock's far corner.

cons.text: On the R408, a corner site between two roads
cons.detail: The gate opens onto the R408 Maynooth–Rathcoffey road, which runs along the front, with a lane along the other side of the paddock; the house sits near the road edge.
€4,474/m², stamp duty about €5,950; with a retrofit and an annex the total would pass roughly €700k (rough).

cons.text: BER E, oil heating, unknown water and drainage
cons.detail: BER E (kWh not published) on a part-stone 1800s house; a heat pump and insulation retrofit is a rough €40–70k before grants. Water and sewer aren't stated.
CHI at Tallaght or Crumlin is about 30 km; Naas and Connolly are closer but take ages 16+ only.

cons.text: Moderate radon risk; heritage status unchecked
cons.detail: BuyerIQ flags moderate radon and five planning applications within 1 km (one active build); protected-structure status of the house and outbuildings wasn't verified.
